verdicts.why: Amal echoes 'Your mouth hurts?', so she heard 'it hurts' (biwja3); بوجع vs بيوجع is a one-vowel engine spelling, not proven first person.
اليوم جمعة is ordinary spoken Levantine for 'today is Friday' and Amal gives no signal; no defensible error.
He stated الكلمات الطبيعات as a sentence (not a question), Amal recast كلمات الطبيعة and said nature has no plural: an invented plural she fixed out loud.
Amal was quizzing 'what do I add?' and his إشي؟ / هو؟ are question-mark guesses at a piece he could not recall; that is a didn't-know, not a slip.
'Is it مسلسلين؟' is a question to her, which the brief rules is neither a slip nor a use; she answered it.
'One would be مبسوط؟' is a question while working out the structure, and Amal only explains the meaning; no wrong form produced in a sentence.
'Is it حشاشيش؟ I forgot the plural' is an explicit question about the plural, so under the brief it is neither a slip nor a use.
His كان at 57:37 comes before her 'Was.' at 57:38, so it is his own self-fix (GR-22).
'Would it be سؤالي آخر إلي؟' is a question about the form after his first try, so it is not a fresh slip (the first try is the only row).
هذه اللعبة was an unfinished start (هذه اللعبة could open a correct sentence), her 'Mm-mm... Yes' is ambiguous, and he restarted to أول لعبة إلي himself.
على ثنتين drops the el- on the clock time (her own chat writes 3ala el-tentain, sheet 3ala elsaa3a tentain); Amal only commented on the number's form and let it pass, a grammar-B slip.
لُعبات؟ is a rising-tone search for a plural he did not know (and لُعب is itself a real plural form); Amal supplied ألعاب, which is a didn't-know, not a slip.
مع الشوق بك is almost surely the engine garbling a goodbye (Amal answers يلا بشوفك), so no word of his can be shown wrong.
